study.title: Proverbs 5 - the danger of seduction and the path of fidelity
study.overview: This chapter contrasts two moral trajectories. In the initial verses, wisdom warns against the immoral woman, whose speech seems sweet, but whose end brings bitterness, loss and death. Then the teaching passes to the practical distance from this temptation: not to get closer to the danger, not to give in to the impulse and to remember that God sees all the ways. In the final part, wisdom presents the positive remedy: joy in legitimate marriage, contentment with the wife herself and continuous fidelity. The chapter ends with a solemn sentence: sin holds the sinner, and lack of discipline leads to death and detour.

outline.title: Listen to wisdom and distrust of seduction
outline.explanation: The master draws the child to pay attention and keep discernment. The immoral woman appears as someone whose speech is pleasant, but whose destiny is deadly. The central point is that the sweet appearance covers a destructive end, so young people should hear and not deviate.

outline.title: Get away early from the wrong way
outline.explanation: The orientation is concrete: to keep away, not even to get closer to the door of her house. The chapter shows the consequences of infidelity: loss of honor, wear and tear of years, unjust use of the fruit of labor and late repentance. The person only realizes late the cost of despising correction and instruction.

outline.title: Satisfy in marriage and theme the righteousness of God
outline.explanation: The image of the cistern's own water teaches exclusivity and joy in the marriage bond. The text values the woman of youth and the constancy of conjugal love. Then it is said that the Lord sees all the ways, and the wicked ends up trapped by the very wickedness and his madness.

study.context: The chapter is a discourse of wisdom addressed to a child, with a special focus on young people. The scores provided indicate that this instruction was aimed at men who began adult and professional life. The theme is treated as a recurring warning of sapiential literature, and teaching focuses on forming discernment, self-control and fidelity in the conjugal relationship.
study.theology: Theologically, the chapter teaches that morality is not only a private matter, but a path of life or death. Sexual sin is described as seducer at first and destructive at the end. There is also a strong emphasis on personal responsibility before God: he observes all the ways and brings real consequences for wickedness. At the same time, wisdom not only forbids; it guides to good, showing that conjugal fidelity is a gift and protection against ruin. The text does not reduce temptation to an external problem: sin also holds the transgressor himself for his choices.

scholarViews.insight: Verses 1 to 2 show that giving attention to instruction produces discernment, especially before an immoral woman.
The chapter makes a solemn warning to young people, treating them as children and calling them to listen attentively to resist the desires of the flesh.
The strange woman is someone who does not belong to her husband, and her lips use misleading, sweet and seductive words.

questions: What signs of seduction appear today with harmless appearance, but hide destructive consequences?
How can the practice of avoiding danger early, and not just resisting at the last moment, change our decisions?
How can fidelity in marriage be seen as a path of joy, and not just of restriction?
study.practice: Practice preventive distance from situations that feed improper desires, rather than negotiate with them. Value the instruction received and ask for discernment before acting. If you are married, cultivate concrete joy in your relationship: time, attention, words of honor and exclusivity. If you are not married, treat purity as serious preparation for future fidelity. In all cases, remember that God sees the whole way, not just the moment of temptation.
study.uncertainty: The given notes do not explain all the poetic details of the chapter, so some images remain interpreted in general. It is also not possible to affirm, based only on notes, more specific historical data on authorship, date or exact environment, besides that the text is a sapiential instruction addressed to young people. Comparison with practices of other ancient wisdom literatures appears in the notes, but without enough details to enlarge beyond that.
